value.rationale: Pendant duplication is a natural graph perturbation with a structural dynamical consequence: it converts all-extinguishing nilpotent XOR cores into reversible systems while deterministically doubling each Jordan-chain length. This yields exact period spectra and populations on infinite graph families. The sharp dyadic path/cycle dichotomy compares nearly equal vertex counts yet finds a factor-two difference in maximal temporal periods. Neither the general Jordan-law nor all-size orbit counts are a textbook restatement of the already credited invertibility result.
